I use the iPhone Mirroring feature every day to quickly access my iPhone right on my Mac, and this year it's getting even better. The public betas of iOS 27 and macOS 27 Golden Gate have launched this month, bringing three major updates to iPhone Mirroring. Here's everything new.

macOS 27: What's New with iPhone Mirroring

The biggest change to iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 is the ability to resize the iPhone Mirroring window.

As my colleague Marcus reported last week, you can now resize the iPhone Mirroring window using any app that supports iOS 27. For now, this means it's limited to Apple's native iPhone apps. However, once developers start rolling out iOS 27 updates later this year, resize support will expand quickly.

Previously, iPhone Mirroring on macOS only supported three preset sizes: Smaller, Actual Size, and Larger. What's Changing in macOS 27 Golden Gate and iOS 27

expected to launch later this year.

There are a few other updates coming to iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 and iOS 27:

  • Access to Control Center
  • DRM video support

Previously, iPhone Mirroring had no access to Control Center at all. In macOS 27, you can access it using the CMD+4 keyboard shortcut, or through the Show menu in the Mac menu bar.

DRM video support means you can watch protected videos through iPhone Mirroring on your Mac. Previously, all DRM-protected videos would only display a black screen when iPhone Mirroring was enabled.

macOS 27 also introduces a new app icon design for iPhone Mirroring, matching several other built-in Apple apps.

How often do you use iPhone Mirroring on your Mac? Are you excited about these changes in iOS 27 and macOS 27? Have you tried them in the public beta? Share your thoughts in the comments.
